To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability of chitosan nanosystems in intestinal fluid is due to the hydration forces that appear between particles in the absence of surface charge and that the stability of these nanosystems is greater when the chitosan chains have low molecular weight and high degrees of acetylations.
the stability of chitosan nanosystems in simulated intestinal fluids is mainly governed by hydration forces and the hydrophilicity and molecular weight of chitosan.
the colloidal stability of chitosan nanosystems in intestinal fluids is mainly due to the hydration forces between the chitosan chains and the ionic strength of the medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of chitosan nanotechnology and its application as a carrier of active ingredients.
the development of a novel and simple method to quantify the chitosan's hydrophilicity, as well as the effect of this property on the stability of chitosan nanospheres.
the development of new nanocapsules with improved stability in intestinal fluids, which is a critical factor to be considered in the development of oral drug delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chitosan shells with a low molecular weight and high hydrophilicity provide better colloidal stability to the nanocapsule system.
, in order to achieve the best results, the chitosan chains should be as hydrophilic as possible and as low in molecular weight as possible.
the stability of chitosan nanosystems in the gastrointestinal tract is mainly due to the hydration forces, which are strongly dependent on the chitosan molecular mass and DA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of chitosan nanosystems is not only dependent on the surface charge but that the hydrophilicity (and the molecular weight) of the chitosans is also important.
, for the design of stable chitosan nanosystems, it is more important the molecular weight of the chitosans than the DA.
chitosan nanospheres with a high degree of acetylation, low molecular weight, and a low degree of polydispersity are the best candidates to provide stability at neutral pH values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of electrostatic repulsive forces, the stability of the chitosans is governed by the hydrophilicity and the molecular weight of the chitosane shell.
chitosan nanomaterials are not only stable under acidic pH values, as previously thought, but also in the neutral intestinal fluids, where the electrostatic repulsion forces are not present.
chitosan nanosystems with low molecular weight, high DA, and high charge density provide the highest colloidal stability.
